Definition
[kappa-noncollapsing at a scale] Source: cao-zhu 1. Definition 3.3.1\group Cao–Zhu No Local Collapsing Theorem I Let $\kappa $, $r$ be two positive constants and let $g_{ij}(t), 0 \leq t <T,$ be a solution to the Ricci flow on an $n$-dimensional manifold $M$. We call the solution $g_{ij}(t)$ $\kappa $-noncollapsed at $(x_0,t_0)\in M \times [0,T)$ on the scale $r$ \index{$\kappa $-noncollapsed} if it satisfies the following property: whenever \[ |Rm|(x,t)\leq r^{-2} \] for all $x \in B_{t_0}(x_0,r)$ and $t \in [t_0-r^2,t_0]$, we have \[ Vol_{t_0}(B_{t_0}(x_0,r)) \geq \kappa r^n. \] Here $B_{t_0}(x_0,r)$ is the geodesic ball centered at $x_0\in M $ and of radius $r$ with respect to the metric $g_{ij}(t_0)$.
